thesis: This episode argues that Uber is a category-defining, fundamental long-only investment with a market cap of $70–$80 billion, now held by institutional players rather than startup founders or hedge funds. The thesis rests on Uber's focused expansion across ridesharing, Eats, and freight segments, alongside new growth bets in suburban markets, international cities, and grocery/liquor fulfillment that aim to outperform Amazon.

claims.claim: The speaker notes that DoorDash has done a good job in urban centers, but implies Uber has a constructive position versus them.
claims.quote: As we built out selection in urban centers, our category position versus DoorDash is actually quite constructive, really strong, we are looking to break into the suburbs.

claims.claim: The speaker acknowledges DoorDash has done a good job, but states it is not the end of the story for Uber.
claims.quote: All of it has to come together, which is difficult, and DoorDash has done a good job. It's not the end of the story, though.

claims.claim: The speaker mentions that Uber has become much more focused on its three core segments: ridesharing, Eats, and freight.
claims.quote: I think now, things have changed, which is we have become much more focused on those three segments.

claims.claim: The speaker states that about 50% of Uber's growth will come from new initiatives that really didn't exist.
claims.quote: If we do it right, 50% of our growth will come from these new initiatives that really didn't exist.

claims.claim: The speaker mentions that a whole new best portfolio will be 35% of Uber's growth.
claims.quote: That whole new best portfolio will be 35% of our growth.

claims.claim: The speaker notes that Uber is expanding into countries like Germany, Spain, Japan, Korea, and Turkey with tweaks to the business model.
claims.quote: We're in Germany, we're in Spain, we're in Japan, we're in Korea, we're in Turkey. There are a bunch of countries that we're expanding into, with tweaks to the business model to make sure that we're expanding into those countries the right way.

claims.claim: The speaker mentions that Uber has a number of growth bets, including the base business Uber X which is going to be 50% of their growth.
claims.quote: If you look at rides, we have a number of growth bets, which is there's this base business, Uber X, which is going to be 50% of our growth.

claims.claim: The speaker mentions that Uber is expanding ridesharing into the suburbs now, and it's a pretty fast-growing part of their business.
claims.quote: Totally. Now we are expanding ridesharing into the suburbs now, and it's a pretty fast-growing part of our business.

claims.claim: The speaker mentions that Uber is expanding into taxi, low cost hailables, two wheelers, three wheelers, Uber for business, health, transportation, all of these different segments.
claims.quote: There's a whole host of new bets that we're making in terms of transportation, taxi, which is huge, low cost hailables, two wheelers, three wheelers, Uber for business, health, transportation, all of these different segments.

claims.claim: The speaker mentions that Uber is expanding into grocery, liquor, et cetera on the Eats side.
claims.quote: But it's really about getting into the other categories, getting into grocery, liquor, et cetera.

claims.claim: The speaker mentions that Uber is separating the tech stack so that they can offer marketplace and fulfillment in a separable way.
claims.quote: Now, we're separating the tech stack, so that now we can offer. We can go to merchants and say, if you want a marketplace, great. But if you want fulfillment, we can offer you fulfillment in a separable way.

claims.claim: The speaker mentions that Uber is aiming to have the local grocer out-Amazon Amazon.
claims.quote: More and more, our vision is we essentially want the local grocer to out-Amazon Amazon.

claims.claim: The speaker mentions that Uber is working with taxis, and that they have become much bigger than taxis.
claims.quote: Our working with taxis was an interesting twist. To some extent, they have been definitionally the competition, or we have been the competition or the challenger to those incumbents. At some point, we became much bigger than taxis.

claims.claim: The speaker mentions that Uber is building a technology blast dispatch for taxi markets, instead of a one to one match.
claims.quote: The team built a technology blast dispatch, which is instead of a one to one match, we'll make a dispatch to 10 different taxis, and one of them accepts.

claims.claim: The speaker mentions that Uber is now in a good place, and the shareholding is moving from startup folks or hedge funds to fundamental long-only players.
claims.quote: I think we're now in a good place, which is the shareholding is moving from either some of the startup folks or hedge funds to fundamental long-only players, who hopefully they'll be shareholders for the next 10 years.
